Review of 3542cb6e7850 / f11834e37011 / 1e20bc257f7c
2026-10-21

Judgements follow independent byte and execution-path inspection. Atomscan
scores, vendor claims, existing repository reviews, and external family names
were leads. No specimen executable or application script was launched. Only
ASPack decompression was emulated, with WinAPI calls replaced by inert stubs;
execution stopped before entering the unpacked VB6 program. The JavaScript
string decoder was separately isolated and bounded in QuickJS.

3542cb6e7850576636ed2b692e6f870f42a2bd6e1f3b4876205a11da57fe0a6e
MALICIOUS: DISM-host carrier containing a VB6 executable binder/autorun worm.

The beginning is the Windows 7 DismHost 6.1.7600.16385 executable. Its first
96,767 bytes equal the corresponding prefix of the 96,768-byte executable
fetched from Microsoft's symbol server:
https://msdl.microsoft.com/download/symbols/dismhost.exe/4A5BC39032000/dismhost.exe
The missing final byte is alignment padding. Entry RVA 0xf3cc initializes the
security cookie then reaches CRT startup 0xf0b8 and WinMain 0x7b54. Its ordinary
DISM/COM servicing behavior does not explain or activate the appended bundle.
This unchanged prefix is insufficient to judge the whole artifact benign.

A raw PE-header walk found 37 starts, including embedded headers inside larger
malformed images. Header starts are not a count of independently executable
payloads. The bundle contains Java launchers, the UPX packer, Office perfboost,
Adobe/Mozilla helpers, App-V mavinject32, setup programs and repeated carriers.
Restoring one missing alignment byte on analytical copies of 22 signed vendor
images made each calculated Authenticode image digest match its signed digest.
Certificate-chain verification still failed in the local trust environment;
these are digest checks, not assertions of current trust. The outer container
has no signature record. Vendor certificates do not sign its appended malware.

At offsets 0x294def, 0x2a6c48, 0x2af9ef and 0x2b49ee are byte-identical
18,429-byte ASPack-packed VB6 images. They declare Firewall.exe/Microsoft
Firewall but name Xiang Corporation; those labels alone prove no behavior.
Their .text/.data/.aspack regions are writable and not marked executable.
The stub starts at VA 0x409001. Manual section mapping was required because
an intermediate image is shorter than its declared final raw section.
Bounded Unicorn emulation restored .text, rebuilt approximately 80 runtime
imports, and reached native entry 0x4014d8. This pushes VB header 0x4024e0 and
calls the recovered runtime entry. Static Capstone and rizin disassembly of
the reconstructed image established the following effects:

- 0x403310 opens the first executable (Open at 0x403356), sizes and reads it
  into an array. 0x403400 similarly reads a second executable (0x40348d).
  0x403540 opens the output at 0x4035aa and writes both buffers through
  __vbaPutOwner3 at 0x4035bb and __vbaPutOwner4 at 0x4035d7. The adjacent
  infection routine selects *.exe at 0x404320. These are file-binding actions,
  not an inferred ransomware encryption operation.
- 0x403a57 creates WScript.Shell. The routine constructs two Variant arguments:
  an HKLM CurrentVersion\\Run entry and its carried patcher executable path,
  then supplies Regwrite and those arguments to __vbaLateMemCall at 0x403b15.
- The drive routine at 0x404420 iterates the supplied drive-letter string.
  It constructs :\\autorun.inf, opens file 5 at 0x40451a, prints [Autorun]
  and Shell=NTDETECT.EXE at 0x404549/0x40455b, then closes it. It constructs
  :\\NTDETECT.EXE and passes the carried image and destination to the runtime
  file-copy primitive at 0x4045c9. Subsequent SetAttr calls modify the created
  files' attributes. The caller supplies a c-through-z drive-letter list.

The recovered drive propagation and Run-key installation tip the verdict.
Not every appended image was demonstrated to execute from the outer entry;
malformed nested hosts and non-executable section flags limit conclusions
about successful execution of this exact container. No unsupported attribution
to all families listed in the collector filename is made. The Triage page
could not be retrieved with the web tool; its score is not verification.

Final raw-byte coverage is two suspicious findings, in section/header and
section/reloc: writable non-executable entry with embedded PEs, and high-entropy
relocation overhang. There are zero hostile findings. The malicious behavior
is established in the manually unpacked code; the original packed bytes do
not expose a sufficiently general behavior matcher. The new notable ASPack
stub fingerprint records verified packer output without calling every ASPack
program malware or elevating structural metadata to meet a hostile quota.

f11834e37011385acbe45cbd9c00cf0a60577ed9a8fc0f751941aec6821d5e81
BENIGN: Atom's Connections 1.7.1 beta, an unsigned .NET messaging host.

Decoded all 17 CIL method bodies with dnfile/dncil, resolving metadata and user
strings. Main -> Run reads application options and checks the resource hash.
LoadFiles reads app.pak, verifies SHA256, GZip-decompresses it and reads
length-prefixed assets into a dictionary. It does not load the bytes as code.
Resource SHA256 db2fd6b4dc620bdddf8cad94e451514066e9cd8181f40ba9a4905159800ccc3c.
Assets: index.html (616,829 bytes), player.html (5,019), PeerJS (92,865).
No native overlay, P/Invoke payload, Assembly.Load or injection chain was found.
Osslsigncode confirms no Authenticode signature; the embedded checksum is not
publisher authentication.

Run generates a 32-byte random device key and saves it with current-user DPAPI.
It decrypts this application's device.key, not another program's credentials.
Listen binds 127.0.0.1/localhost, default port 47800. Handle validates Host;
/save and /device-key require POST, X-Atoms:1 and a non-cross-site request.
SafeTarget validates path components and restricts writes to the application's
Pictures/Documents roots. OpenBrowser launches the local URL via Process.Start.
EndOtherCopies is called on bind failure, queries its own executable basename,
excludes its PID, compares the port, and kills only the stale matching instance.
RegisterProtocol writes a per-user atoms: URL handler; MakeDesktopShortcut uses
WScript.Shell for a visible desktop link. Neither implements login persistence.

The HTML has custom-alphabet Base64, array rotation and arithmetic lookup
wrappers. Isolated evaluation of only J, C, the rotation and 1,140 pure wrappers
replaced 10,968 constant lookup calls. The application itself was not evaluated.
Traced the decoded WebCrypto, IndexedDB vault, PeerJS startup, session handshake,
received-message dispatcher, file saves, backups, calls, updates and plugins.
Identity plus ephemeral P-256 ECDH secrets derive AES-GCM session keys via HKDF.
Received frames enforce sequencing; admission requires a known contact or a
valid invitation. Dispatch handles messages, posts, groups, files and calls,
not operator-provided host commands. PBKDF2 belongs to user-created backups.
The separate player was decoded and permits fixed YouTube/Vimeo playback
commands, with parent and embedded-player origin/source checks.

Fetched and inspected the actual referenced services and dependencies:
https://unpkg.com/peerjs@1.5.4/dist/peerjs.min.js
  Byte-identical to bundled PeerJS (SHA256
  ad5d8870d1e389914f9cba8d35be313c4327c69ee0a221e482e9bf7621136fe5).
  The configured 0.peerjs.com:443 broker is ordinary WebRTC signaling.
https://atomsconnections.com/
https://atomsconnections.com/version.json
https://atomsconnections.com/Atoms-Connections.zip
  The current distribution is 1.11.0, a different executable; it is supporting
  product context, not a hash match for 1.7.1. Its README describes the recovered
  local-browser, invitation and file-sharing flows. The older sample's updater
  accepts same-origin HTTPS download metadata and offers a click to download;
  it does not execute the installer.
https://atomsconnections.com/plugins/catalog.json
  Downloaded both current plugins, Neon Arcade and Atom Math Lab. Both hashes
  equal their catalog SHA256 values. Static scripts implement games, arithmetic
  answers, display/audio, local progress storage and app-mediated messaging.
  Neon Arcade's bundled rendering library has ordinary resource fetch helpers;
  these do not establish a hidden command channel. Plugins are opt-in archives
  whose hashes are checked and whose HTML is mounted in an allow-scripts iframe
  without same-origin authority. Injected CSP denies network connections and
  nested frames. Additional application permissions start disabled.

The actual flows support the advertised application, without recovered
credential theft, hidden native tasking, attacker endpoint or preconfigured
hostile peer. Unsigned distribution, compressed assets, JavaScript obfuscation,
DPAPI, WMI process termination, COM and registry APIs plausibly explain generic
loader/stealer heuristics. The source's precise collection reason, publisher
history and host deployment authorization are unavailable. This BENIGN verdict
is an evidence-limited artifact judgement and takes sighted quarantine under
the queue policy. All accurate capability traits remain.

1e20bc257f7c637a95f935d613d9a9c17eede935f3ed96c1edd8c96c1cf6403e
BENIGN: stock XMRig 6.26.0 with a 64-byte unmapped trailer.

Fetched the official static Linux x64 release:
https://github.com/xmrig/xmrig/releases/download/v6.26.0/xmrig-6.26.0-linux-static-x64.tar.gz
Archive SHA256 fc6f8ae5f64e4f17481f7e3be29a1c56949f216a998414188003eae1db20c9e5
agrees with https://github.com/xmrig/xmrig/releases/tag/v6.26.0.
The enclosed 8,350,992-byte xmrig has SHA256
b20f39fc00d242e706b6c30367ad811c676e0575050a4ec2f30104b696944b49.
Every one of those bytes equals the sample prefix. The addition is 64 opaque
bytes after the original section-header table, outside loadable segments.
Headers, executable code, data, initializers and the entry point are unchanged.
No meaning or hostile activation is assigned to the unexplained trailer.

Rizin traces 0x40e5f3 -> C runtime -> main 0x40d280, Process construction at
0x459d30 and CLI dispatch at 0x458c60, then App construction 0x501040 and exec
0x501650. Compared these paths with the official v6.26.0 App.cpp, Process.cpp,
Config_default.h and Msr_linux.cpp. The readiness failure returns 2; success
handles background/dry-run settings, starts configured mining and enters libuv.
The share-submission path builds mining.submit requests. At 0x605236 the MSR
initializer attempts allow_writes, then passes /sbin/modprobe msr allow_writes=on
with output redirection to system() when necessary. These are existing-permission
mining tuning operations, not an elevation exploit. CPU/DMI inventory, hugepages,
Stratum, donation/benchmark services, TLS and optional HTTP API match upstream.
Libuv process helpers explain execve, signal, session and UID/GID capabilities;
no backdoor is inferred merely because those library primitives are linked.

No code modification, injected pool/wallet, persistence installer, Mirai attack
or propagation code was recovered. Standard configuration is external; no
operator configuration or live process arguments accompanied this sample.
The systemd-like filename and unexplained tail warrant investigation on a host.
Cryptojacking incidents often use stock XMRig, plausibly explaining hostile
corpus provenance and miner AV labels. Without an installer, service, command
line, configuration, ownership/consent or host timeline, the available artifact
does not establish unauthorized mining. The BENIGN judgement goes to sighted
quarantine; it is not a claim of benign deployment. Retain all mining, network,
crypto, module-command, permission and process capabilities.

Trait corrections and verification

- Added metadata/build/protector::aspack-x86-unpacking-stub: a general ASPack
  startup fingerprint, scoped to its PE section and actual i386 COFF machine.
  Architecture inference alone did not reject a sparse ARM control. The final
  inline YARA matcher explicitly binds header and section. It detects producer
  output, not malicious intent or a family, and uses no specimen filename,
  campaign string, hash or exact file size.
- Moved ProcessStartInfo's .text name observation from symbols/descriptor to
  symbols/name. A class-name token is not a type-descriptor shape. Its matcher,
  description, severity, platforms and file scope are unchanged; every active
  exact YAML consumer follows the new ID.
- The target name directory was at 100 rules. Its structured Go Cmd.Start API
  symbol is a process capability, so it moves to process/create/spawn with
  unchanged matcher/scope/severity. The raw .gopclntab name remains metadata.
  The sole exact consumer follows it; the existing umbrella's two alternatives
  and truth value are preserved. No descriptor/name directory selector is
  active. Shared ancestor selectors keep their observations. The build ancestor
  consumers are JavaScript-only and cannot gain this PE-only fingerprint.
  The spawn-directory consumers are source/script scoped; the broader timing
  consumers require a C#-only date atom and cannot gain the native Go atom.
  The shared process/create ancestor already contains the unchanged Go
  umbrella, so its broad presence consumers retain their old truth value.
- Twelve inert PE/ELF controls verify packer sequence vs name-only, broken
  get-PC bytes, section and architecture near misses; ProcessStartInfo name,
  absence and section scope; and real Go symbols vs strings/near names/pclntab.
  Four additional internal evaluations verify the existing Go umbrella. That
  any-only umbrella is omitted from rendered output by the engine, so testing
  its internal match separately is necessary. All 16 checks pass.
- Initial atomscan and cleave facts were run for all three inputs; speculative
  decoded candidates were examined without treating transforms of ordinary
  text as proof of obfuscation. Final local rescans retain two suspicious and
  zero hostile traits in the native bundle, zero of either in both benign
  artifacts, and add the ASPack fingerprint to the packed VB6 unit. Final
  atomscan is repeated with this checkout selected through CLEAVE_TRAITS_DIR.
